English Literature.question: ১) An apparently self-contradictory statement that hides a rational meaning is called-
English Literature.exp:
- An apparently self-contradictory statement that hides a rational meaning is called paradox.
- Some example of paradox:
• The world will be saved by failure.
• Cowards die many times before their deaths.
• There is no one so poor as a wealthy miser.
• Sweet are the uses of adversity.
• The world will be saved by failure.
• Ignorance is strength.
• I must be cruel only to be kind.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ২) 'The secret of success is the constancy of purpose' was said by-
English Literature.exp:
- Francis Bacon is the Father of English Essay and Father of Modern Prose.
- His famous quotations:
- The secret of success is the constancy of purpose.
- Wonder is the seed of knowledge.
- Reading maketh a full man, conference a ready man, written an exact man.
- Opportunity makes a thief.
- It is impossible to love and be wise.
- History makes man wise.
- Studies serve for delight, for ornament and for ability.
- Some books are to be tasted, others to be swallowed, and some few to be chewed and digest of studies.
- Silence is the sleep that nourishes wisdom.
- Revenge is a kind of wild justice.
- Unmarried men are best friends, best Masters, best servants but not always best subjects.
- Old wood best to burn, old wine to drink, old friends to trust and old authors to read.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and The Oxford Dictionary of Quotation.

English Literature.question: ৩) The longest period of English literature is-
English Literature.exp:
• The longest period of English literature is 'The Anglo-Saxon Period'.
• The duration of this period is 450 to 1066 (616 ages).
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৪) 'They think too little who talk much' was said by-
English Literature.exp:
• John Dryden is the Father of Modern English Criticism.
• His famous quotations:
- They think too little who talk much.
- Jealousy is the proof of love.
- We first make our habits then habits make us.
Source: The Oxford Dictionary of Quotation.

English Literature.question: ৫) 'Time is money' is an example of-
English Literature.exp:
- Metaphor is an implicit comparison between two different things.
- যখন কোনো বাক্যে দুটি ভিন্ন বা বিজাতীয় জিনিসের মাঝে পরোক্ষভাবে বা রূপকার্থে তুলনা করা হয় তাকে বলা হয় Metaphor।
- যেমনঃ Time is money.
- My life is local bus.
- Life is but a walking shadow.
- Revenge is a wild justice.
- The world's a stage.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৬) 'The course of True love never did run smooth' is taken from the writings of-
English Literature.exp:
• A Midsummer Night's Dream is a famous comedy by William Shakespeare.
• Famous quotations of this comedy:
- The course of True love never did run smooth.
- My soul is in the sky.
- Love looks not with the eyes but with the mind.
Source: The Oxford Dictionary of Quotation.

English Literature.question: ৭) 'The Barren Period' of English literature is-
English Literature.exp:
- The Middle English Period of English Literature is divided into 3 short periods.
• The Anglo Norman Period (1066-1340),
• The Age of Chaucer' (1340-1400) and
• The Dark or Barren Period (1400-1485/1500).
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৮) 'He prayeth best who loveth best, All things both great and small' was said by-
English Literature.exp:
• Samuel Taylor Coleridge was a Romantic poet.
• He is known as 'Poet of Supernaturalism'.
• His famous quotations:
- He prayeth best who loveth best, All things both great and small.
- 'Alone, alone, all, all alone;
Alone on a wide, wide sea!
And never a saint took pity on
My soul in agony'
- 'Water, water, everywhere;
And all the boards did shrink;
Water, water, everywhere;
Nor any drop to drink'
Source: The Oxford Dictionary of Quotation.

English Literature.question: ৯) 'Dramatic monologue' is used in-
English Literature.exp:
- A kind of lyric poem in which a single speaker expresses his thoughts and feelings to an imaginary listener.
- 'Dramatic monologue' is used in Poetry.
- Robert Browning excels in dramatic monologue in English literature.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ১০) The duration of 'The Age of Shakespeare' is-
English Literature.exp:
• The Renaissance Period (1500-1660) is divided into 4 main Periods. Such as
- Elizabethan Period (1558-1603),
- Jacobean Period (1603-1625),
- Caroline Period (1625-1649) and
- Commonwealth Period (1649-1660).
• 'The Puritan Age' refers to (1620-1660).
• The duration of 'The Age of Shakespeare' is 1590 to 1616.
Source: Live MCQ lecture and An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ১১) 'Sweet is Revenge - especially to women' is taken from the writings of-
English Literature.exp:
• Lord Byron is the rebel poet of English literature.
• His famous quotations:
- Sweet is Revenge - especially to women.
- Man's love is of man's life a thing apart, Tis (it is) women's whole existence. (Don Juan)
- Men's conscience is the Oracle of God,
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and The Oxford Dictionary of Quotation.

English Literature.question: ১২) 'Willy Loman' is an important character of-
English Literature.option1: ক) The Old Man and the Sea
English Literature.option3: গ) For Whom the Bell Tolls
English Literature.exp:
• 'Death of a Salesman' is a famous play which is written by Arthur Miller.
• Important character of this play:
- Willy Loman,
- Biff Loman,
- Howard Wagner,
- Linda Loman,
- Happy Loman,
- Charley etc.
Source: Death of a Salesman by Arthur Miller.

English Literature.question: ১৩) A literary term used to describe a satire or comedy is called-
English Literature.exp:
- A literary term used to describe a satire or comedy is called farce.
- A group of performers who comment together on the main action in a play.
- Diction is the choice of words in literature.
- Hymn is a religious song or poem in praise of God.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ১৪) Find an odd man out.
English Literature.exp:
- Rudyard Kipling is a modern British Novelist.
- P. B. Shelley, Lord Byron and John Keats are the poets of the Romantic Age.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ১৫) 'Our birth is but a sleep and a forgetting' is taken from the writings of-
English Literature.exp:
• William Wordsworth is a famous Romantic poet.
• His famous quotations:
- 'Our birth is but a sleep and a forgetting',
- 'Child is the father of man',
- 'Nature never did betray the heart that loved her',
- 'Poetry is a spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings',
- 'Poet is the breath and finer spirit of knowledge',
- Every great poet is a teacher.
- 'Come forth into the light of things, let nature be your teacher'.
Source: The Oxford Dictionary of Quotation.

English Literature.question: ১৬) 'Mosca' is a important character in-
English Literature.exp:
• Volpone is a famous play which is written by Ben Jonson.
• It's important characters:
- Volpone,
- Mosca,
- Celia,
- Voltore,
- Corbaccio,
- Castrone
- Bonario,
- Corvino etc.
Source: Encyclopedia of Britannica and Volpone by Ben Jonson.

English Literature.question: ১৭) Which period is known as 'The Golden Age of Lyrics'?
English Literature.exp:
• The Romantic Period is also known as 'The Golden Age of Lyrics' and 'The Age of Revolution'.
• The slogan of this age is 'Art for Art's Sake'.
• The Romantic age of English Literature is 1798 to 1832.
• This period belongs to Nineteenth century.
• The characters of this Age:
- Subjectivity,
- High Imagination,
- Supernaturalism,
- Love for nature,
- Love for beauty,
- Simplicity etc.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ১৮) 'Charms strike the sight but merit strikes the heart' was quoted by-
English Literature.exp:
• Alexander Pope is a Mock Heroic Poet.
• His famous quotations:
- 'Charms strike the sight but merit strikes the heart',
- 'A little learning is a dangerous thing',
- 'To err is human, to forgive is divine',
- 'An honest man is the noblest work of God',
- 'The proper study of mankind is man',
- 'Fools rush in where angels fear to tread',
- 'Hope springs eternal in the human breast'.
Source: The Oxford Dictionary of Quotation.

English Literature.question: ১৯) The Renaissance Period was started from
English Literature.exp:
- The Renaissance Period (1500-1660) is divided into 4 main Periods.
- So, this period started from 1500.
- This period is divided into 4 main periods.
• Elizabethan Period (1558-1603),
• Jacobean Period (1603-1625),
• Caroline Period (1625-1649) and
• Commonwealth Period (1649-1660).
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ২০) 'Catherine Earnshaw' is an important character of-
English Literature.exp:
• Wuthering Heights is a famous novel which is written by Emily Bronte.
• Important character of this novel:
- Catherine Earnshaw
- Cathy Linton,
- Edgar Linton,
- Heathcliff,
- Lockwood etc.
Source: Wuthering Heights by Emily Bronte.

English Literature.question: ২১) What is an epic?
English Literature.exp:
An epic is a long narrative poem that tells in grand style the history and aspirations of a national hero.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ২২) 'Where ignorance is bliss, it is folly to be wise' is stated by-
English Literature.exp:
• Thomas Gray is known as a Graveyard poet.
• His famous quotations:
- Where ignorance is bliss, it is folly to be wise.
- Full many a flower is born to blush unseen, And waste its sweetness on the desert air.
- The paths of glory lead but to grave.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and The Oxford Dictionary of Quotation.

English Literature.question: ২৩) The inversion in the order of words or phrases when repeated is called-
English Literature.exp:
The inversion in the order of words or phrases when repeated is called Chiasmus.
Examples:
- 'Beauty is truth, truth beauty'.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

Chiasmus is a rhetorical device in which two or more clauses are balanced against each other by the reversal of their structures in order to produce an artistic effect. 
For Example:
“Never let a Fool Kiss You or a Kiss Fool You.”

English Literature.question: ২৪) Dr Aziz is an important character of-
English Literature.exp:
• 'A Passage to India' is a famous novel of Edward Morgan Forster.
• Important Characters of this novel:
- Dr Aziz,
- Miss Adela,
- Ronny Hislop,
- Stella Moore,
- Turton,
- Callender,
- Cyril Fielding etc.
Source: A Passage to India by E. M. Forster.

English Literature.question:
২৫) 'If Winter comes,
Can spring be far behind?' was stated by Shelley in-
English Literature.option4: ঘ) Ode to the West Wind
English Literature.exp:
• P. B. Shelley is a famous Romantic poet.
• His famous quotation:
- 'If Winter comes, can spring be far behind?' (Ode to the West Wind),
- 'The more we study, the more we discover our ignorance' (Queen Mab),
- 'Fear not the future, weep not for the past' (Queen Mab),
- 'Our sweetest songs are those that tell of saddest thought' (Ode To A Skylark),
- 'Poets are the unacknowledged legislators of the world' (A Defence of Poetry).
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopedia of Britannica.

English Literature.question: ২৬) Which one is not a writer of Victorian age?
English Literature.exp:
• A list of writers of 'Victorian Age':
- Charles Dickens,
- Thomas Hardy,
- Matthew Arnold,
- Lord Alfred Tennyson,
- Robert Browning,
- George Eliot,
- Samuel Butler etc.
• Jane Austen is a writer of the Romantic Age.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ২৭) 'There are two tragedies in life. One is not to get your heart's desire. The other is to get it.' was stated by-
English Literature.exp:
• G. B. Shaw is the greatest Dramatist of modern English literature.
• His Important quotations:
- 'Beware of false knowledge; it is more dangerous than ignorance'.
- 'It is our duty to live as long as we can',
- 'Nine shoulders out of ten are born fools',
- 'God is on the side of big battalions',
- 'There are two tragedies in life. One is not to get your heart's desire. The other is to get it.'
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and The Oxford Dictionary of Quotation.

English Literature.question: ২৮) 'John Tanner' is an important character of-
English Literature.exp:
• Man and Superman is a famous play which is written by G. B. Shaw.
• Important character of Man and Superman:
- John Tanner,
- Hector Malone,
- Ann Whitefield,
- Mendoza,
- Roebuck Ramsden,
- Octavius Robinson,
- Violet Robinson,
- Susan Ramsden etc.
Source: Man and Superman by G. B. Shaw.

English Literature.question: ২৯) 'The woods are lovely, dark and deep' was quoted by-
English Literature.exp:
• Robert Frost is an American national poet.
• His famous poem is 'Stopping by woods on a snowy evening'.
• Famous quotation of this poem:
- ''The woods are lovely, dark and deep,
But I have promises to keep,
And miles to go before I sleep,
And miles to go before I sleep.''
- 'Good fences make good neighbors' (Mending Wall).
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopedia of Britannica.

English Literature.question: ৩০) The duration of 'Jacobean Period' is-
English Literature.exp:
- The Renaissance Period (1500-1660) is divided into 4 main Periods. Such as-
• Elizabethan Period (1558-1603),
• Jacobean Period (1603-1625),
• Caroline Period (1625-1649) and
• Commonwealth Period (1649-1660).
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৩১) 'Give me liberty, to know, to utter, to argue freely, according to conscience above all of my liberties' is quoted by-
English Literature.exp:
• John Milton is a great Master of verse in the puritan period.
• He is a famous Epic poet in English literature.
• His famous quotations:
- Give me liberty, to know, to utter, to argue freely, according to conscience above all of my liberties.
- 'Childhood shows the man as morning shows the day',
- 'It is better to reign in hell than to serve in heaven'
- 'Love quarrels of in pleasing Concord end.',
- 'Death is the golden key that opens the place of eternity'.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and The Oxford Dictionary of Quotation.

English Literature.question: ৩২) The literary term 'Euphemism' means-
English Literature.exp:
- Euphemism is a figure of speech which stands for a pleasant way of referring to something unpleasant.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.
- ইংরেজি সাহিত্যে 'Euphemism' শব্দের অর্থ সুভাষণ, কোমল প্রকাশ (inoffensive expression)।
- অর্থাৎ অস্বাভাবিক বা কঠোর বা কর্কশ শব্দের বদলে কোমল, মৃদু বা শ্রুতিমধুর শব্দের ব্যবহার। যেমনঃ
- 'Kick the bucket' is an euphemism that describes the death of a person.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৩৩) 'Popular opinion is the greatest lie' who quoted this line?
English Literature.exp:
• Thomas Carlyle was a Scottish philosopher.
• His famous quotations:
- Popular opinion is the greatest lie.
- Speech is great, silence is greater.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and The Oxford Dictionary of Quotation.

English Literature.question: ৩৪) 'Cordelia' is an important character of-
English Literature.exp:
• King Lear is a famous tragedy of William Shakespeare.
• The important character of this tragedy:
- King Lear,
• Three daughters of an arrogant king:
- Goneril,
- Regan and
- Cordelia.
- Edgar etc.
Source: King Lear and Encyclopedia of Britannica.

English Literature.question:
৩৫) 'Alone, alone, all, all alone;
Alone on a wide, wide sea' is an example of-
English Literature.exp:
- The Repetition of a vowel sound in nearby words (without the recurrence of consonant sounds which would make a rhyme).
- Alone, alone, all, all alone;
Alone on a wide, wide sea' is an example of Assonance.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৩৬) 'The success is not mine, the failure is not mine, but the two together make me' is taken from the writings of-
English Literature.exp:
• Charles Dickens is the greatest novelist in the Victorian Period.
• His famous Novel is Great Expectations.
• Famous quotations of great expectation:
- The success is not mine, the failure is not mine, but the two together make me.
- Charity begins at home and Justice begins next door.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and The Oxford Dictionary of Quotation.

English Literature.question: ৩৭) 'Lieutenant Frederic Henry' is the protagonist of-
English Literature.exp:
• 'A Farewell to Arms' is a famous novel of Ernest Hemingway.
• Important character of this novel:
- Lieutenant Frederic Henry (Protagonist),
- Catherine Barkley,
- Lieutenant Rinaldi,
- Helen Ferguson,
- Miss Gage etc.
Source: Encyclopedia of Britannica and A Farewell to Arms.

English Literature.question: ৩৮) 'The best way to destroy an enemy is to make him a friend' was quoted by-
English Literature.option1: ক) A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
English Literature.exp:
• Abraham Lincoln was a former president of the USA.
• His famous quotations:
- The best way to destroy an enemy is to make him a friend.
- Marriage is neither heaven nor hell, it is simply purgatory.
- The ballot is stronger than bullet.
- Democracy is the government of the people, by the people, for the people.
- With malice towards none, with charity for all.
- You can fool all the people some of the time, and some of the people all the time, but you cannot fool all the people all the time.
Source: Encyclopedia of Britannica.

English Literature.question: ৩৯) An exaggerated statement or an extreme overstatement is called-
English Literature.exp:
- An exaggerated statement or an extreme overstatement is called Hyperbole.
- 'Ten thousand saw I at a glance' is an example of Hyperbole.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question:
৪০) 'All the world's a stage
And all the men and women are merely players.' is quoted by William Shakespeare in-
English Literature.exp:
• 'As You Like It' is a famous comedy by William Shakespeare.
• The important questions of this comedy:
- 'All the world's a stage
And all the men and women are merely players.'
- 'Sweet are the uses of adversity'
- Love is merely a madness.
- To the last gasp with truth and loyalty.
- I'll have no husband, if you be not he.
- 'Under the greenwood tree who loves to die with me, and turn his merry note.'
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and As You Like It.

English Literature.question: ৪১) In which century was the Romantic Period?
English Literature.exp:
- The Romantic age of English Literature is 1798 to 1832. This period belongs to the Nineteenth century.
- The Victorian age of English Literature is 1832 to 1900.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৪২) 'Portia' is an important character of-
English Literature.exp:
• The Merchant of Venice is a famous comedy by William Shakespeare.
• Important character of this Tragedy:
- Shylock,
- Portia,
- Antonio,
- Bassanio,
- Jessica etc.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and The Merchant of Venice.

English Literature.question: ৪৩) 'To be or not to be that is the question' is the beginning of a famous soliloquy from-
English Literature.exp:
• Hamlet is a Tragedy written by William Shakespeare.
• Famous quotation of Hamlet:
- 'To be or not to be that is the question',
- 'Frailty, thy name is woman',
- Brevity is the soul of wit',
- Neither a borrower nor a lender be; For loan off loses both itself and friend',
- 'There is divinity that shapes our end',
- 'There are many things in Heaven and Earth, Horatio, than are dreamt of in your philosophy.'
- 'I must be cruel, only to be kind: thus, bad begins and worse remains behind.'
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopedia of Britannica.

English Literature.question: ৪৪) 'Puffs, powders, patches, Bibles, billet-doux' is an example of-
English Literature.exp:
- The Repetition of a consonant at the beginning of two or more words or stressed syllables is called Alliteration.
- 'Puffs, powders, patches, Bibles, billet-doux' is an example of Alliteration.
- Here 'p' has been repeated thrice and 'b' twice.
- Fair is foul, and foul is fair.
- Ruins seize thee, ruthless king!
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৪৫) 'Fagin' is an important character of-
English Literature.exp:
• Oliver Twist is a famous novel which is written by Charles Dickens.
• Important character of this novel:
- Oliver Twist,
- Fagin,
- Bill Sikes,
- Nancy,
- Agnes Fleming,
- Charley Bates etc.
Source: Oliver Twist and Encyclopedia of Britannica.

English Literature.question: ৪৬) 'Dream is not that, which you see while sleeping; It is something that will not let you sleep' Who quotes this line?
English Literature.exp:
• A. P. J. Abdul Kalam was a former president of India.
• His famous quotations:
- ''Dream is not that, which you see while sleeping; It is something that will not let you sleep''.
- ''If you want to shine like the sun, first burn like it''.
Source: Autobiography of A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

English Literature.question: ৪৭) Who is the poet of 'The Restoration Period'?
English Literature.exp:
• Some poet of 'The Restoration Period':
- William Congreve,
- John Milton,
- John Dryden,
- John Locke,
- John Bunyan,
- Samuel Butler etc.
• Poet of The Augustan Period:
- Alexander Pope,
- Jonathan Swift,
- Daniel Defoe,
- Samuel Richardson etc.
• Robert Herrick is a poet of The Caroline Period.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৪৮) 'A man can see farther through tear than a telescope' is quoted by-
English Literature.exp:
• Alfred Tennyson is a famous Victorian poet.
• His famous quotations:
- A man can see farther through tear than a telescope.
- Knowledge comes but wisdom lingers.
- Sorrows are the best educator.
- The old order changeth yielding place to new.
- Authority forgets a dying king.
- Who are wise in love, love most, say least.
- I will never rest from travels, I will drink life to the lees.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and The Oxford Dictionary of Quotation.

English Literature.question: ৪৯) 'Iago' is a famous character of William Shakespeare taken from-
English Literature.exp:
- Othello is a famous Tragedy of William Shakespeare.
- Important Character of Othello:
• Othello,
• Desdemona,
• Brabantio,
• Iago,
• Cassio etc.
Source: Othello and Encyclopedia of Britannica.

English Literature.question: ৫০) 'Make me immortal with a kiss' is quoted by-
English Literature.exp:
• Christopher Marlowe is the father of English Drama or Tragedy.
• His famous quotation:
- Sweet Helen, make me immortal with a kiss.
- Man is the maker of his own fate.
- There is no sin but ignorance.
Source: Encyclopedia of Britannica.
